architecture.title: How AI4SMB Insights is built
architecture.subtitle: The system that powers the platform, in plain terms.

rows.implementation: Next.js 16 (App Router) with React 19 and Tailwind CSS, server-rendered, deployed on a global edge network; internationalized English / Simplified Chinese.
rows.what: Available through an ordinary browser; no installation or account required.

rows.implementation: A set of stateless API services covering generation, segmentation, the conversational strategist, post formatting, image generation and review retrieval.
rows.what: Separate API routes organize these capabilities; shared providers can affect multiple features.

rows.implementation: Provider-abstraction layer routing to an open-weight model, gpt-oss-120b, served on LPU inference hardware, with Google Gemini 2.5 Flash / Pro as an alternate route, selected per request.
rows.what: No hard dependency on any single model vendor; models are interchangeable behind one interface.

rows.implementation: Gemini has per-process minute/day request limits and can fall back to Groq on quota errors. Generation and segmentation have separate in-memory session rate limits.
rows.what: Helps control requests; these are not a global spending cap or a guarantee of fail-over on every error.

rows.implementation: PostgreSQL (Supabase) with row-level security enabled on every table; migration-controlled schema; anonymous session model with optional authenticated accounts via magic link.
rows.what: Tenant isolation and least-privilege access; use without an account is the default.

rows.implementation: CSV and POS input is parsed in the browser. Recognized identifying columns are removed; column statistics, computed cohort counts and sanitized sample rows are sent for analysis.
rows.what: The original file is not uploaded. Heuristic redaction may miss identifiers in unfamiliar columns or free text; review inputs before analysis.

roadmap: Self-hosted inference on vLLM, so model serving runs on infrastructure we operate rather than third-party APIs.
Domain-specialized open-weight models, fine-tuned with parameter-efficient adapters on consented, de-identified data.
Automated detection and redaction of residual identifiers in free-text input.
Differential-privacy techniques for cross-business industry benchmarks.
Independent security assurance, including a SOC 2 examination.
architecture.footerLinks: Read more about how <privacy>customer data is handled</privacy> and the <model>models behind the platform</model>.

privacyPage.title: How we handle your data
privacyPage.subtitle: We minimize the data sent for analysis and describe both the safeguards and their limits.
privacyPage.flowTitle: What happens when you upload a file

flowSteps.title: Your browser
flowSteps.desc: The file is read and parsed on your own device.

flowSteps.title: Identifying fields removed
flowSteps.desc: Recognized name, email and phone columns are removed; detectable email and phone patterns in text are masked.

flowSteps.title: A minimized summary is sent
flowSteps.desc: Column distributions, sampled non-identifying values, and derived segment features.

flowSteps.title: Analysis returns
flowSteps.desc: Segments and suggestions return. The original file stays on your device, but sanitization is heuristic and may miss residual identifiers.

controls.body: CSV and POS input is parsed in the browser. Recognized identifying columns are removed; column statistics, computed cohort counts and sanitized sample rows are sent for analysis. The original file is not uploaded. Heuristic redaction may miss identifiers in unfamiliar columns or free text; review inputs before analysis.

The platform is fully usable with no account. An anonymous session identifier, not a person, is the default unit of record; signing in is optional and exists only so you can retrieve your own saved work.

controls.lead: Tenant isolation at the database layer.
controls.body: Schema scripts enable row-level security. Server-side service-role requests bypass RLS, so account routes also scope their queries to the authenticated user.
Privileged keys exist only server-side and are never exposed to the browser; the client holds only a public, restricted key.

Generation and segmentation apply in-memory limits when a session identifier is supplied. The public benchmark API has a separate limit. These controls are not a comprehensive abuse-prevention guarantee.
The interface states in plain language, at the point of upload, exactly what is processed locally, what is transmitted, and what is retained.

We do not run a training or fine-tuning pipeline on uploads. Analysis is sent to configured third-party inference services; their handling is governed by applicable service terms and account settings.
Export covers your profile, linked sessions, campaigns and segments. Deletion removes these records but does not delete the authentication account or promise erasure of every log or backup.

privacyPage.footerLinks: See how these controls are enforced, and where our security and privacy work is going next, in the <arch>system architecture</arch>.

modelCard.title: Model card
modelCard.subtitle: Which models power this platform, and why they are open.

models.name: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI)
models.role: Primary generation: segmentation, campaigns, conversational strategist, post formatting

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash / Pro
models.role: Alternate route, selected per request for capacity and fail-over

whyOpen: Open-weight models provide an additional option for controlling inference costs and supporting a free core service.
A provider abstraction reduces dependence on a single hosted model, although providers can still change prices and availability.
The model, its weights and its behavior can be audited, which the platform's explainability commitments depend on.
modelCard.selectionP1: A provider-abstraction layer means a model can be substituted by configuration rather than a rewrite.
modelCard.selectionP2: The codebase includes a model-comparison harness. A complete marketing-quality evaluation across all candidate model families has not yet been established.
modelCard.explainabilityBody: Prompts request reasons for recommendations; this alone does not validate their truth. For recognized CSV date/order-value fields, code computes and preserves cohort counts and rules independently of generated marketing suggestions. Other inputs and all creative suggestions still require review.
limitations: Outputs are generated text and should be reviewed before publication.
Benchmark segments for a business type and location are estimates, not measurements of that specific business.
The platform does not have access to a business's live ad performance unless the owner provides it.
Generated figures and statistics in marketing copy should be verified by the owner.
modelCard.trainingDataBody: We do not run a training or fine-tuning pipeline on uploads. Analysis is sent to configured third-party inference services; their handling is governed by applicable service terms and account settings.
